seo_title: Beauty and the Beast Story and Lesson — A Classic About True Beauty
meta_description: The story and lesson of Beauty and the Beast, the original tale, plus read-aloud tips for teaching your child about inner beauty. A classic-tale guide for ages 4–7.

content.alt: Belle and the Beast meeting in the castle
content.text:
What kind of tale is Beauty and the Beast?

Beauty and the Beast is the story of Belle, a girl who ends up staying in the castle of a fearsome beast, who discovers the true heart beneath his appearance and breaks the spell with love. It's a French classic carrying the message that true beauty lies within.
content.caption: Seeing beyond appearances

content.text:
The original story of Beauty and the Beast

The version refined in 1756 by the French author Madame de Beaumont is the most widely known. The heart of it is a bond that begins with a single rose, life in the beast's castle, and the ending in which the beast returns to being a prince through Belle's heartfelt love.
content.caption: A rose that marks the time

content.alt: The beast turned back into a prince
content.text:
Story summary of Beauty and the Beast

Belle, who stays in the beast's castle in her father's place, is afraid of the beast at first, but as they live together she comes to know his gentle, true heart. Belle's heartfelt love breaks the spell, the beast returns to his handsome prince form, and the two live happily ever after.
content.caption: The spell that love broke

content.text:
The lesson Beauty and the Beast teaches

The heart of it is that you should look at the heart, not the appearance, and that sincerity and love overcome prejudice. Talk with your child about "Have you ever met a friend who looks scary but has a warm heart?"
content.caption: An ending where hearts connect

content.text:
How to read it aloud to your child

Change your voice for the beast—heavy at first, then warm once their hearts connect. Use "Why did Belle stop being afraid of the beast?" to point out how important it is to see what's inside. Best suited for ages 4–7.
content.caption: Reading that looks at the heart

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is Beauty and the Beast good for?
A. It's best suited for ages 4–7. With its themes of inner beauty and overcoming prejudice, it's great for emotional development.

Q. Won't the beast be scary?
A. The version for young children draws the beast in a non-threatening way and has a warm ending, so children can watch with ease.

Q. What conversations are good to have?
A. Talk together about "not judging by appearances" and "a friend with a warm heart."
